glossary.Chronic pain disorder: A condition causing pain that persists or recurs for months or longer.
glossary.Ophthalmic: The V1 branch of the trigeminal nerve, supplying forehead and eye.
glossary.Innocuous stimuli: Normally harmless sensations, such as light touch or a breeze.
glossary.Intermittent: Coming and going rather than constant.
glossary.Electric-shock-like: Sudden, sharp, stabbing pain like an electric shock.
glossary.Neurological deficit: Loss of function in part of the nervous system, such as numbness or weakness.
glossary.Red flags: Features suggesting a serious underlying cause needing investigation.
glossary.Secondary cause: An underlying disease, such as MS or a tumour, causing the symptoms.
glossary.Gold standard: The most accurate, definitive way to make a diagnosis.
glossary.Clinical diagnosis: A diagnosis made from history and examination without needing tests.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: a scan using magnets, best for showing brain and nerve detail.
glossary.Tumour: An abnormal growth of tissue, benign or malignant.
glossary.Structural compression: Pressure on a nerve from a physical structure, such as a vessel or mass.
glossary.Anticonvulsant: A drug used to prevent seizures; some also treat nerve pain.
glossary.Sodium channel: A membrane pore letting sodium into nerve cells to fire an action potential.
glossary.Hormonal contraception: Contraceptives using hormones, such as the pill, implant or patch.
glossary.Side effect: An unwanted effect of a drug.
glossary.Referral: Sending a patient to a specialist team.
glossary.Nerve root: The part of a nerve where it leaves or enters the brainstem or spinal cord.
glossary.Focal demyelination: Loss of the myelin sheath at one spot along a nerve.
glossary.Myelin: The fatty insulating sheath around nerve fibres that speeds and separates signals.
glossary.Action potential: The electrical impulse that travels along a nerve.
glossary.Cross-talk: Signals jumping between neighbouring nerve fibres that have lost insulation.
glossary.Demyelinating plaques: Areas of myelin loss in the brain or spinal cord, typical of MS.
glossary.Neuronal membranes: The outer membranes of nerve cells that carry electrical signals.
glossary.Stabilise: Make nerve membranes less likely to fire.
glossary.Neurology: The medical specialty for brain, spinal cord and nerve disorders.
